subject.title: chore(pr): dev-wrapper opt-in — advisory subcommands may dogfood modified wrappers

question: Should a committed but unmerged local `scripts/pr` implementation be allowed to trigger `ci-dispatch`, or should canonical code remain mandatory for repository automation commands?
rationale: The branch preserves the default behavior but intentionally authorizes an opt-in exception for a command that creates external GitHub Actions work; source review cannot decide the acceptable maintainer trust model.

options.title: Keep CI dispatch canonical
options.body: Remove `ci-dispatch` from the advisory classification and retain the new local-wrapper path only for non-mutating inspection such as `ls`.

options.title: Approve controlled dogfooding
options.body: Retain `ci-dispatch` as advisory and explicitly accept that maintainers may run committed pre-merge wrapper code to dispatch CI from their own credentials.

recommendation.title: Keep CI dispatch canonical
recommendation.body: Remove `ci-dispatch` from the advisory classification and retain the new local-wrapper path only for non-mutating inspection such as `ls`.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current `ci-dispatch` behavior and authored the proposed trust-boundary exception.
